messages:
maria-sales: quick one — Acme asks for short-lived hosted API keys for a 2-week POC. They want rotation every 24h, easy revocation, and proof of audit logs. Can we give them a standard flow they can operationalize?

aj-eng: yep. we have a lightweight flow for hosted POCs. summary: create ephemeral key (TTL configurable), optionally allowlist CIDRs, monitor usage in console, and revoke via API or Console if needed. will share exact commands. cc @vivian-se for sales handoff details.

vivian-se: thanks. also need to confirm billing impact — customer worried about accidental token leak driving cost. any recommended limits?

aj-eng: put a rate limit + usage quota on the API key for the POC. on hosted keys you can attach usage caps: e.g., 100k tokens/day. For leaks, immediate revocation + rotate to new key. we can provide a short playbook for non-engineers.

maria-sales: perfect. can you paste the commands/snippets we should give them?

aj-eng: here you go — create ephemeral key (example):
```
POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/admin/keys
Authorization: Bearer <ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "type": "ephemeral",
  "expires_in": 86400,    // seconds (24h)
  "scopes": ["inference:generate"],
  "note": "acme-poc-ephemeral-1",
  "usage_limits": {"tokens_per_day": 100000}
}
```
Use expires_in to control TTL. For a 2-week POC, rotate keys daily or every 24h.

aj-eng: revoke example (console or API):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/admin/keys/revoke \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <ORG_ADMIN_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"key_id":"<KEY_ID>"}'
```
The Console UI also has a one-click "Revoke" on the key detail page.

vivian-se: can we include an IP allowlist snippet? they will host POC servers within a corporate NAT.

aj-eng: yes — you can attach an allowlist on the key metadata. sample: 
```
"allowlist": ["203.0.113.0/24", "198.51.100.45/32"]
```
This is enforced at the API gateway; requests from other IPs are rejected (401).

riley-security: note from security: for enterprise POCs we recommend MFA on admin accounts, short key TTL (<=24h), and logging to an external SIEM if they require retention >30d. we also need to approve any service account that will create keys programmatically.

maria-sales: who owns the programmatic create flow? customer wants automation to rotate keys every night.

aj-eng: two options: 1) we create ephemeral keys via the admin API from the customer's automation runner (they store the org-admin token in their pipeline) — not ideal. 2) we provide a delegated service account with limited scope that can issue ephemeral keys via a restricted endpoint. option 2 is safer. we'll coordinate with security for the service-account ACL.

vivian-se: ok i'll scope this in the SOW: daily rotation, 100k tokens/day cap, IP allowlist, & immediate revocation procedure. can we also provide a short incident playbook (who to ping)?

aj-eng: yes — playbook snippet: 
- If suspected leak: revoke key immediately (API/Console).
- Create replacement ephemeral key and update clients.
- Check audit trail in Console -> Keys -> Activity (shows create/revoke and originating admin).
- If abuse suspected, open support ticket with `priority=security` and include key_id + timestamps.

deploy-bot: audit-log: created key acme-poc-ephemeral-1 by org-admin at 1971234567 (simulated).

riley-security: also add a postmortem template for leaks: root cause, blast radius, remediation, and follow-up controls.

maria-sales: this is great. last: how quick is revocation effective? customer asked if an attacker can use a revoked token for a few minutes.

aj-eng: revocation is immediate at the gateway: any token revoked returns 401 on next request. however, active streaming sessions will be cut at next token check — usually sub-second to a few seconds. if they need extra assurance, shorten TTL to 1h and use rotation.

vivian-se: i'll bundle this into a one-page playbook to send to Acme and attach the sample commands. thanks all — i'll follow up after I get their security questionnaire. :thumbsup:
